summary.headline: UFlex Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to Rs 6,265 mn at a 15.3% margin, the highest in 14 quarters, though management flagged spreads moderating in Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.8% QoQ and 5.7% YoY to Rs 40,973 mn, with EBITDA up 36.3% QoQ and 31.8% YoY to Rs 6,265 mn. Management attributed the jump to a March spike in film spreads, as raw material increases were more than passed through. For FY26, revenue grew 2.1% to Rs 155,130 mn and EBITDA rose 8.1% to Rs 19,836 mn, with margin up 70 bps to 12.8%. Management said spreads for BOPET and BOPP have since moderated significantly, and it declined to give an FY27 EBITDA margin range.

financial_highlights.change: Management said it expects a similar level going forward; analyst cited Rs 378 crore for FY25 base, management referenced Rs 700 crore last fiscal, figures were inconsistent on the call

segments.name: Packaging Films
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 128,037 MT, +11.4% QoQ and +0.9% YoY; FY26 volume fell 1% to 498,034 MT. Americas volume 31,883 MT (+23% QoQ, +18% YoY); Europe 35,367 MT (+12.9% QoQ, soft YoY); India 26,888 MT (+6.3% QoQ, -6.3% YoY); MEA 33,899 MT (+4.6% QoQ, +1.5% YoY).

segments.name: Packaging Solutions / Packaging (incl. aseptic, holography)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 38,842 MT, +7.1% QoQ and +1.6% YoY; FY26 volume up 5.1% to 151,755 MT. Aseptic packs rose 15.9% QoQ; FY26 aseptic volume 7.97 bn packs, +2.4%. Packaging Solutions is about 36% of revenue and about 40% of FY26 EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Company expects FY27 performance to be better than FY26, driven by better utilisation of new capacity, product mix and capacity coming online in FY27.
Aseptic FY27 sales volume guided to about 10.0-10.5 bn packs, up from about 8 bn in FY26, including part-year contribution from the Egypt 12 bn facility.
Management declined to give an FY27 EBITDA margin range, citing Q1 still in progress.
Margin outlook: non-film packaging margins expected to hold; packaging film margins expected to moderate with industry trends, especially in India.
Roughly Rs 1,900-2,000 crore of the Rs 2,169 crore consolidated CWIP expected to be capitalised during FY27.
capex_capacity: Aseptic 12 bn-pack facility in Egypt expected to commission in H1 FY27; remaining capex about Rs 972 crore.
WPP bag facility in Mexico (mainly for US pet food) expected to commission in H1 FY27; remaining capex largely incurred. Installed WPP capacity about 80 mn bags.
PET recycling facility (rPET 36,000 MT and rMLP 3,600 MT) commissioned at Sector 155 at end of April 2026; ramp-up over next three quarters; Rs 47 crore remaining capex incurred.
54,000 MTPA BOPP line at Dharwad, India, expected to commission in FY27-28; significant capex in FY26-27. Manufacturing line capex about Rs 700 crore, mostly in FY26 and FY27.
Sanand (India) aseptic debottlenecking to 12 bn packs achieved in Q3 FY26. CWIP at March 2026 Rs 2,169 crore consolidated.
demand_pricing: In Q4, raw material (PET chips, BOPET and BOPP homopolymer) prices rose sharply in March, but market prices rose more, so spreads widened and some additional spread was realised.
Spreads have since moderated significantly, particularly for BOPET, and are well below Q4 levels as raw material prices softened and market prices fell.

Americas demand recovered after the US government shutdown; Europe demand soft YoY on weak CPG demand and cheaper imports; India film demand hit by customers deferring purchases amid price-correction expectations.
International revenue is 57% of total and India 43%; the mix has shifted toward overseas over the past year.
Egypt benefited from localised sourcing as supply chains were disrupted in the region.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread outlook for BOPP and BOPET, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads spiked in March and widened in Q4, but have moderated significantly in Q1 FY27, especially for BOPET; utilisation rose sequentially in Q4 and management will watch it closely given price softening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation, finance cost and capitalisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated depreciation and finance cost were each about Rs 787 crore and Rs 777 crore, with both expected to remain at similar levels. Roughly Rs 1,900-2,000 crore of CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage come down and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to net debt/EBITDA improving from 4.51x in Q3 to 4.35x in Q4, which excludes EBITDA from projects yet to commission, and expects further improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aseptic volume outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aseptic volume expected at about 10.0-10.5 bn packs versus about 8 bn in FY26, including part-year Egypt contribution; FY26 utilisation about 80% plus on the 12 bn capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-film packaging margins expected to hold, film margins may moderate. Blended cost of funds about 9% (was above 9%); refinancing is premature, with cheaper overseas funding expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company commit to an EBITDA margin range for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it was too early in Q1 to give an annual EBITDA range and would track margin developments closely.

risks_watch: Film spreads have moderated sharply from March peak; Q1 FY27 margins at risk, especially in India films.
Commissioning timelines for Egypt aseptic (12 bn) and Mexico WPP facilities (H1 FY27) and the ramp-up of rPET/rMLP capacity.
Leverage at 4.35x net debt/EBITDA and about Rs 8,500 crore debt; monitor leverage as new capacity contributes EBITDA.
Q&A on aseptic packaging: a PIL and litigation involving liquor packaging in some states; management declined to quantify exposure.
Shareholder-value question on the stock's valuation and promoter stake; management said it respects market price and would convey the suggestion to promoters.
Inconsistent finance cost figures stated on call (Rs 378 crore vs Rs 700 crore for FY25); verify against filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and the new capacity, but noticeably cautious on Q1 FY27 margins and spreads, and evasive on FY27 EBITDA range, WPP pricing and liquor-related aseptic exposure. Management also declined to quantify several analyst questions.
key_quotes: both the aggregate EBITDA recorded during the quarter and also the EBITDA margin achieved was the highest in the last 14 quarters, which was after Q1 of FY23.

the company expects to perform better in FY27 than FY26, driven by improved utilization of recently commissioned capacities, product mix optimization and additional capacities expected to come online during FY27.
I think it will be a little premature to give a sense of what kind of EBITDA range will be there for the year as a whole.
